selectedLaw: CapabilityAvailabilityNoticeV1 carries the COMPLETE ownership tuple in TYPED fields - capabilityId, languageMode, workspaceRoot as UserInputPath - never concatenated, because workspaceRoot is bounded at 4096 while BoundedText is 1024.
code is `const native.capability-unavailable`, an EXISTING registry member already aliased from provider-unavailable/capability-missing.

No notice is discarded and no invocation-wide request cap is imposed.

capability-availability is a DECLARED parityField of every requestClass=analysis command - all five, including repair-verify - so every applicable renderer carries it, and declared means REQUIRED.

twoItemDispositions.regressionIIntroducedAndFixed: I had added `if k in envelope['parity']` to render so an old fixture would pass, which silently weakened the inherited required-field behavior for EVERY parity field. Strict access is restored with the reason recorded in the code; section 8's existing conversion stands - a missing declared field is operational-failed / DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED with faultCause delivery-required, retaining a committed RunId, and the helper exception alone is not a public termination.

twoItemDispositions.wasWrong: 14 of 16 branch targets were PROSE that refuses the real DomainDetail schema, none of the keys was in internalAliases, my recordsEditOwnedByRoot claimed every target was already a member and the edit was mechanical, and my own control whitelisted `request detail`/`operational record` prefixes so it could not fail. StepTermination admission alone also did not complete the surface: a kind=failure envelope requires a NONEMPTY errors array, so routes leaving domainDetail absent refused. Guard output is colon-suffixed and had no normalizer; the preview-* guard emitted prose the normalizer correctly refused; a 4096-character mode produced a 4149-character subject that made the envelope schema-invalid.
selectedLaw: public_termination_for(key, origin) derives a real StepTermination for every branch; failure_envelope_errors composes the required errors array - exactly the termination's detail where it has one, the route's envelopeDetail where it does not.

Origins per admission section 1 and the inherited D9 law: external configuration -> request-rejected/CONFIG.INVALID; externally supplied or retained spec of KNOWN external origin -> request-rejected/REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED; host BUG minting its own invalid internal layer -> operational-failed/SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE with faultCause host-invariant (nonAnalysisDerivation rule 5, domainCondition host-fault); authenticated release declaration -> request-rejected/REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED; producer boundary -> operational-failed/PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. A NOT-SELECTED cell is ORIGIN-INDEPENDENT: REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE with the existing PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED detail. Each key declares the boundaries it can arise at and refuses any other.

normalize_internal_key matches the LONGEST registered key followed by a colon; the remainder is the subject; an unregistered raw string refuses. Every guard emits a registered key - the preview-* guard now raises native.release-capability-preview-constant:<id>.

bounded_subject elides over-long subjects: raw is a UNICODE SCALAR STRING, length and slicing count CODE POINTS (what BoundedText's maxLength counts), the SHA-256 input is raw.encode('utf-8') with no normalization, 64 lowercase hex after the ASCII marker `...#sha256:`, result exactly 1024 code points. Distinct values are distinguished under the ORDINARY collision-resistance assumption, and the guarantee is confined to what is PUBLISHED - no separate retained store is promised or named.

Four public DomainDetailCode members are ADDED - native.capability-spec-invalid, native.release-declaration-invalid, native.coverage-cause-unsupported, HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED - because those routes had no code naming their remedy; reuse was taken where honest (CONFIG.INVALID, PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED). Registry and the generated enum are in lockstep at 287.
Only the two genuinely CONTEXT-FREE keys are aliased; the aliasRule now says a missing alias is a positive statement, not an omission.

Selected D9 composition published in product source: inherit v1.14 UNCHANGED plus exactly the faultCause host-invariant mapped to the EXISTING SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE. The host-INVARIANT subtype specifically was unrepresentable; other host-fault causes always existed. `total and injective` is a property of the declared cause domain, so an orphaned errorCode was never a totality violation - my earlier claim was wrong. Existing classes, exit codes, reason codes and error codes are unchanged, but faultCause DOES grow by one, and saying otherwise would be false.
